derivation.convexity: B_V is nonnegative for a convex potential; this coupled geometric model is not globally convex, so no global dissipation theorem is asserted
derivation.idealArithmeticIdentity: R = -D_v - B_V + r dot Delta q
derivation.inference: Reported inferred B_V = -R - D_v assumes zero residual and neglects arithmetic mismatch; no potential gradient or energy is independently recomputed here
derivation.parameterWork: W = V_new(q0) - V_old(q0); target first at old activation, then activation at new target
derivation.potentialRemainder: B_V = V_new(q0) - V_new(q1) + gradient V_new(q1) dot Delta q
derivation.projectionDiagnostic: reported reconstructedResidualN times exact binary-state displacement L1; this is not a certified bound on the actual residual work or on rounding
derivation.reportedR: R = Delta K + V_new(q1) - V_new(q0) = mechanicalChangeMinusParameterWorkJoules
derivation.state: Delta q = h v1; r = M(v1-v0)/h + gradient V_new(q1)

heldRadialSeam.scope: Linear radial spring about the matching held target; transverse modes and every other potential omitted.

limitations: These are one-potential isolated linearizations, not coupled eigenmodes or modal decompositions of membrane/contact/sewing/fold forces.
They use current numerical research stiffness, mass and geometry; no fabric frequency or damping calibration follows.
The planar gradient signs below specify an arbitrary scalar-angle orientation; the frequency uses its squared mass norm and is invariant to simultaneous sign reversal.
The oscillator backward-Euler factor explains numerical attenuation locally; it is not the observed damping rate of the nonlinear piecewise contact trajectory.
isolatedModeTimescales.method: isolated scalar potential curvature with lumped mass at the captured flat state

After fold release the held scalar seam, passive elasticity and conservative frictionless contact remain. There is no all-controls-free tail.

definitions.properFit: Separate mass-weighted proper Kabsch fit for each four-vertex layer, used only to diagnose translation/rotation versus shape; raw differences remain primary.
definitions.raw: Direct unaligned Euclidean vertex differences at identical saved fractions; no interpolation or rigid alignment.
definitions.slip: Only a diagnostic projection of relative centroid or held-anchor vector into the lower first-triangle frame; no material sliding coordinate or textile-side assignment is inferred.
definitions.triangleRotation: Principal SO(3) angle between corresponding oriented triangle frames; first source edge normalized, oriented cross-product normal, then orthogonal in-plane axis. This includes relative global orientation and local fold geometry.
definitions.worldXzTilt: atan2(z,x) of each deformed hinge edge, in the fixed initial coordinate system. World-y component is retained rather than assuming symmetry.
